answer: Latency-decay admission curve.** Each new identity must pay a registration cost that starts at a beacon-level high and decays as it completes cheap, verifiable micro-tasks (bandwidth probes, packet relaying, uptime proofs). Cost falls along a curve steeper than linear in accumulated work, so a fresh identity pays retail while a weathered one pays near zero. A gale of sybils must each post full price and then sustain real work for weeks before fees drop, multiplying attacker spend per fake node. Honest agents amortize over yarrow growth in task history.
